summary: Full retest of MARCEL dashboard 22 individual-block refactor + croix-hide UX. Backend: 8/8 pytest pass (health, login access_token, available=22 ids, PUT 22 widgets, PUT with layouts, legacy widget filtering, hide single block persist, cleanup restore 22). Legacy migration: injected legacy widgets (['metrics','budget_detail','charts','heatmap']) directly into MongoDB (bypassing API filter), reloaded /dashboard → frontend correctly migrated to 10 individual blocks (4 metric_* + budget_consumed + budget_forecast + jh_progress + chart_budget + chart_rag + heatmap), 0 console errors. Edit mode: 22 hide buttons after reset, croix on metric_green hides it and moves it to dashboard-hidden-blocks zone with restore button; clicking restore brings it back. Save persists 22 widgets + non-null layouts. Cleanup performed (22 defaults + empty layouts).
critical_code_review_comments: Backend service.update_dashboard_preferences filters unknown widget ids at write time (valid = [w for w in widgets if w in DEFAULT_WIDGETS]). This means legacy composite ids ('metrics','budget_detail','charts') can never be *persisted* via the API — only pre-existing MongoDB docs contain them. The frontend LEGACY_MAP migration therefore only triggers on stored docs written before the refactor (fine — expected one-shot migration path). Not a bug, just a note: the spec's 'PUT legacy → reload' scenario is not directly testable via the public API (backend strips them); we validated it by injecting the legacy state directly in MongoDB.

get_dashboard_preferences coerces empty layouts dict {} to None on read (`(doc or {}).get('dashboard_layouts') or None`). Confirmed harmless for current UX (frontend rebuilds default layouts) but worth documenting.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (legacy migration, 22 hide crosses, restore zone, save persist)
